name: Ashwagandha
summary: An Ayurvedic herb (Withania somnifera) whose root extracts are taken mainly to ease stress and anxiety and to improve sleep.
what_it_is: Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) is an evergreen shrub long used in Ayurvedic and Unani medicine, where it is classed as an adaptogen. Most supplements contain root extracts; KSM-66 is a root-only extract and Sensoril uses root and leaf. Its effects are thought to come mainly from steroidal lactones called withanolides, with alkaloids and other components possibly contributing.

evidence.why: Several small, short placebo-controlled trials, mostly in India, report less stress, anxiety and sleeplessness, but results vary widely and a 2026 meta-analysis rated the certainty very low.

status_us.label: Dietary supplement (banned in Denmark)
status_us.note: Sold as a dietary supplement in the US. Denmark banned ashwagandha in 2023 after a 2020 risk assessment, and in 2024 France's food safety agency advised groups including pregnant and breastfeeding women and people with endocrine disorders not to use it.

benefits.claim: Lower stress and anxiety scores, less sleeplessness and lower cortisol than placebo in a review of 7 trials (491 adults in India, 6 to 8 weeks); a 2026 analysis of 22 trials agreed but rated the certainty very low
Small improvement in sleep, larger in people with insomnia and with 8 or more weeks of use (5 trials in India)
May raise testosterone, and in a small trial of people with subclinical hypothyroidism it lowered TSH and raised thyroid hormone levels

risks.risk: Mild stomach upset, loose stools, nausea and drowsiness
Liver injury with jaundice and itching, starting 2 to 12 weeks after use began; in a series of 5 cases none had liver failure, and liver tests normalized within 1 to 5 months in the 4 followed up
Overactive thyroid (thyrotoxicosis) in case reports, which resolved after stopping
Some experts advise against use in pregnancy because of reports of possible miscarriage, though the American Herbal Pharmacopoeia says there is no evidence it causes abortion
Long-term safety is unknown; it appears well tolerated for up to about 3 months

avoid_if: Liver disease or past liver injury from a supplement
Thyroid disease or taking thyroid hormone (clinician first)
Taking sedatives, immunosuppressants, or diabetes or blood pressure medicines (clinician first)
interactions: Thyroid hormone medicines: may interact, and ashwagandha may itself change thyroid hormone levels
Diabetes and blood pressure medicines: may interact

labs.why: No routine tests are needed, but yellow skin or eyes, itching, nausea or unusual tiredness should prompt liver tests, and people with thyroid conditions may need their thyroid levels rechecked.

studies.title: Effects of ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) on mental health in adults: A systematic review and dose–response meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
studies.people: 1,391 adults in 22 randomized trials (India, USA, Australia, Iran)
studies.finding: Ashwagandha lowered stress, anxiety and depression scores versus placebo, but results varied widely between trials, publication bias was detected and certainty was rated very low.

studies.title: Effect of Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) extract on sleep: A systematic review and meta-analysis
studies.people: About 400 adults in 5 randomized trials in India
studies.finding: A small but significant improvement in overall sleep, larger in people with insomnia and with 8 or more weeks of use; no serious side effects were reported.

studies.title: Ashwagandha-induced liver injury: A case series from Iceland and the US Drug-Induced Liver Injury Network
studies.people: 5 people with liver injury in Iceland and the US
studies.finding: Jaundice and itching began 2 to 12 weeks after starting ashwagandha; no one had liver failure, and liver tests returned to normal within 1 to 5 months in the 4 people followed up.

ask_your_clinician: Could ashwagandha affect my thyroid or interact with my thyroid, diabetes, blood pressure or sleep medicines?
Which liver symptoms should make me stop it and call you?
Is my stress or sleep problem one that needs a different treatment?

notes_for_editor: Most trials are small, short and run in India. The 2026 meta-analysis reports unusually large pooled effect sizes, very high heterogeneity and some internal inconsistencies, so it is cited only for direction and certainty. Participant counts for the sleep meta-analysis differ (ODS says 372; the paper's abstract says 400). LiverTox's ashwagandha chapter could not be opened (bot check); the liver risk is sourced to a published case series and ODS. Denmark's ban and France's advice are sourced through ODS, not the agencies themselves.
